# Release v0.1.13 (dev → main)

**Work item:** LP-0MSQ0NI7K009UDE8 · **Type:** chore · **Priority:** medium

> **Retrospective record.** The release executed on 2026-08-12; this intake formalises its definition and verification. No implementation is expected.

## Problem statement

Changes accumulated on `dev` in the `llm-manager` project needed promoting to `main` through the gated ship workflow, so that v0.1.13 becomes a tagged, published release and the `in_review` work items it contains are closed. The release has already run; the work item was left at `stage=idea`, so this brief records what the release was and how it is verified.

## Users

- **Release operator / maintainer** — "As a maintainer I want `dev` promoted to `main` through the gated ship workflow, so the release is deterministic and downstream work items close cleanly."
- **Consumer of the released code** — "As a consumer I want an immutable, tagged `v0.1.13`, so I can pin to a released version."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The release PR is merged into `main` — verified by `gh pr view 20`: state `MERGED`, merge commit `00d656ff88378499f88c81718cf91bc6c84fe921`. *(met)*
- Tag `v0.1.13` exists on `origin` and is an ancestor of `origin/main` — verified by `git ls-remote --tags origin v0.1.13` (present) and `git merge-base --is-ancestor v0.1.13 origin/main` (true). *(met)*
- `package.json` version is bumped `0.1.12` → `0.1.13` — verified by `git show v0.1.12:package.json` (`0.1.12`) and `git show v0.1.13:package.json` (`0.1.13`). *(met)*
- `CHANGELOG.md` is regenerated with a `## v0.1.13 (2026-08-12)` section — verified by `git show v0.1.13:CHANGELOG.md`. *(met — section present; body empty, see Risks)*
- `dev` is synced with `main` after the merge — verified by the release audit comment recorded on this item. *(met)*
- Candidate `in_review`/`completed` work items are closed with the note `Shipped in v0.1.13` — verified by `wl search "Shipped in v0.1.13"` (47 items). *(met)*
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. *(met — release notes carried by PR #20 and `CHANGELOG.md`)*
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. *(met — pytest 2181 passed; node suite passed)*

## Constraints

- The release is executed by `run-release.js` (ship skill); agents never push directly to `main`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is managed exclusively by the ship pipeline and is not hand-edited.
- Resolution is retrospective: no code, config, or pipeline changes are made under this item.

## Existing state

- Release executed 2026-08-12; the repository has since advanced through v0.1.19.
- This is the only release-record item still at `stage=idea`/`status=in-progress`. The ship close step (step 12) only closes `in_review`/`completed` items — a record created at `stage=idea` is never terminalised, so it lingers in the backlog.
- Verification evidence:
  - `gh pr view 20` → state `MERGED`, `mergedAt` 2026-08-12T11:37:12Z, merge commit `00d656ff88378499f88c81718cf91bc6c84fe921`.
  - `git ls-remote --tags origin v0.1.13` → `0bf4f3edb4c13af8c8a2f32fc60bc3e089084404`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor v0.1.13 origin/main` → true.
  - `git show v0.1.12:package.json` → `0.1.12`; `git show v0.1.13:package.json` → `0.1.13`.
  - `git show v0.1.13:CHANGELOG.md` → `## v0.1.13 (2026-08-12)`.
  - Gate summary recorded in the description: unmerged-branches ✓, critical-items ✓ (no open critical), worklog-refs ✓, tests ✓.

## Desired change

- **No functional change.** Formalise this item (this brief) and let the standard lifecycle terminalise a historical release record. Where the producer prefers, it may be closed directly as `done` rather than driven through planning/implementation, since every acceptance criterion is already satisfied.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — `version` field, bumped `0.1.12` → `0.1.13` by `release/bump-version.js`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `## v0.1.13` section generated by `release/generate-changelog.js`.
- `.worklog/` — release audit comment and closed-item bookkeeping (managed via `wl` only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** this item is a retrospective release record, not future work; no implementation is expected. Recorded here so the lifecycle can close it without generating spurious work.
- **Risk (realised):** the `## v0.1.13` changelog section is empty, so release notes exist only in PR #20. This is the same class of defect as LP-0MUEALIM60037F1S (empty v0.1.18/v0.1.19 changelogs). It is a historical artifact, not newly actionable under this item.
- **Risk (realised):** ship `getCandidateItems()` used `set -o pipefail` under `dash` (`/bin/sh`), silently emptying the audit/producer-review gates and the close step. Tracked and fixed in LP-0MSQ0NTMO00577UJ.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not re-run or re-release v0.1.13, and do not backfill historical changelogs under this item; raise separate work items instead.

## Related work

- LP-0MSQ0NTMO00577UJ — ship `getCandidateItems()` `set -o pipefail`/dash defect (discovered-from this release).
- LP-0MUEALIM60037F1S — release post-step ran without a release; mislabelled items and empty changelogs.
- PR https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/llm-manager/pull/20 · tag `v0.1.13`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does this item require an interview?** — Not asked. The seed context (the release description plus git/GitHub evidence) was sufficient to draft a complete brief. Research: verified PR #20 merge state, the `v0.1.13` tag's ancestry of `origin/main`, the version bump, and the changelog section via `gh`/`git`.
- **Q: Should a seven-week-old, superseded release record be driven through the lifecycle, or closed directly?** — **OPEN QUESTION (for producer).** Assumption taken: it is formalised here and later terminalised as a shipped historical record. If the producer prefers immediate closure as `done`, no further work items are needed.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MU9ZXFQS0023DXT** – Post-restart startup ramp: gate new chat requests with 503 + Retry-After (thundering-herd mitigation) (completed)
- **LP-0MSQF2TGU004SXKH** – Quality Improvement - Refactoring (completed)
- **LP-0MUD3A4Q000313D3** – Validate: downtime dispatcher per-slot owner-lease gate in cheap mode (proxy per-slot identity contract) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: affected, audit, automated, bin, close (+43 more)
- `ds4/tests/long_context_security_prompt.txt` — matched: audit, automated, bin, branches, close (+42 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: audit, bin, bump, close, closed (+41 more)

# Intake Brief: When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer (LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI)

> **DRAFT — awaiting producer answers to the OPEN QUESTIONs in the Appendix.**
> The scope below is the agent's proposed reading of the seed intent; the
> alternatives are listed in Q1/Q2 of the Appendix.

## Headline

When the proxy rejects a request because no model/provider/slot can serve it,
the error response must carry a machine-readable retry instruction
(`Retry-After` header **and** a matching `retry_after` JSON field) so a client
can automatically re-issue the request when capacity returns, instead of
surfacing an opaque error. The generic and time-window exhaustion 503 paths
already do this; this item closes the remaining "no models available" paths
that do not, and defines the shared contract they must all satisfy.

## Problem statement

Clients reach an upstream LLM through this proxy. When every model that can
serve a request is unavailable — all providers in the fallback chain are in
cooldown, outside their `available_times` window, or usage-limit quarantined,
or all local slots are busy — the proxy rejects the request. For an unattended
agent (herdr worker / Pi session) to recover automatically, the rejection must
tell it *how long* to wait. The generic and time-window exhaustion 503 paths
already emit a truthful `Retry-After` header and `retry_after` body field
(LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4, LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G), but some capacity rejections still
omit any retry instruction, so a client cannot distinguish "retry in N
seconds" from a terminal error.

The most clearly documented gap is the **local slot-exhaustion 429**:
`proxy/README.md` states it returns the JSON body *"(no `Retry-After`
header)"*. The **router concurrency-limit 503** (`Server overloaded: N
queries active. Retry later.`) also returns no `Retry-After`/`retry_after`.

## Users

- **Local agent (herdr worker / Pi session)** — the primary beneficiary.
  Receives a capacity rejection and needs a concrete retry instruction so its
  recovery classifier can wait and retry, rather than surfacing
  `Unrecognized error:` or hammering the proxy.
- **Proxy operator / on-call engineer** — needs every capacity rejection to be
  self-describing (which capacity was missing, and when to come back) so the
  response alone explains an overnight failure.

### Example user stories

- As an agent whose request hits local slot exhaustion, I want the 429 to tell
  me how many seconds to wait, so I retry automatically when a slot frees up.
- As an agent whose request is rejected because the server is overloaded, I
  want the 503 to carry a retry timer, so my recovery loop backs off instead of
  retrying immediately.
- As an operator, I want every "no models available" rejection to use the same
  `Retry-After` + `retry_after` contract, so I can reason about (and document)
  a single behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

Proposed scope (see Q1/Q2): bring the remaining proxy capacity rejections up to
the existing retry-hint contract.

- **AC1 — Shared contract:** Every response that rejects a request because no
  model/provider/slot can serve it includes both a `Retry-After` HTTP header
  (integer delta-seconds) and a `retry_after` JSON body field, with the **same**
  non-negative integer value.
- **AC2 — Local slot exhaustion (429):** `_build_exhausted_response(all_local_slot_exhaustion=True)`
  includes `Retry-After` + `retry_after`, derived from real capacity (at minimum
  `server.slot_unavailable_retry_after`), consistent with the existing
  `_build_slot_exhaustion_response` 503. Verified by a unit/integration test
  asserting status `429`, `code == "all_slots_exhausted"`, and the header/body
  retry value.
- **AC3 — Router concurrency limit (503):** The concurrency-limit rejection
  (currently `HTTPException(503, detail="Server overloaded: N queries active.
  Retry later.")`) includes `Retry-After` + `retry_after`. Verified by a test
  asserting status `503` and the retry hint.
- **AC4 — Truthful, not hardcoded:** `retry_after` is `0` only when capacity is
  genuinely available; otherwise positive. For slot exhaustion it is bounded by
  the configured slot retry value; for concurrency it reflects a documented
  bound. Verified by tests.
- **AC5 — Additive-only contract:** The existing human-readable `error` prose
  and stable `code` values (`all_exhausted`, `outside_time_window`,
  `all_slots_exhausted`) are unchanged; only the retry instruction is added.
  Verified by the existing exhaustion-contract tests still passing.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation:** At least one automated test per patched path
  asserts the status code, `Retry-After` header, `retry_after` body field and
  `code`.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `proxy/README.md` (the slot-exhaustion
  contract currently documents "no `Retry-After` header"), and any relevant
  wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC8 — Full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive-only:** do not remove or reword existing `error` prose or `code`
  values — older clients key on them (epic constraint LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO).
- **Do not change availability policy:** `available_times` windows are
  intentional; do not wake a provider outside its window to satisfy a retry.
- **No proxy restart:** changes ship through the normal build → test → commit
  workflow; never kill the proxy as part of the fix.
- **Client-side classifier changes are out of scope in this repo** — the
  ContextHub recovery/retry modules live in the ContextHub repository (see Q3
  and Related work).

## Existing state

- Generic exhaustion 503 (`_build_exhausted_response`) and time-window 503
  (`_build_time_window_exhausted_response`) in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` already
  emit `Retry-After` + `retry_after`, computed by `_compute_retry_after` from
  real availability (cooldowns, window edges, usage-limit resets).
- 429 local slot exhaustion (`_build_exhausted_response(all_local_slot_exhaustion=True)`)
  emits `{"error": "All providers exhausted", "code": "all_slots_exhausted",
  "message": "Model server busy: 0/N slots available. Retry later."}` with **no**
  `Retry-After` header and **no** `retry_after` field. `proxy/README.md` documents
  this gap explicitly.
- The router concurrency-limit rejection (`proxy/proxy/router.py`, ~line 1055)
  returns a bare `HTTPException(503, "Server overloaded: N queries active.
  Retry later.")` with no retry hint.
- The sibling `_build_slot_exhaustion_response` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`)
  is the reference implementation: it already sets `Retry-After` and
  `retry_after` from `server.slot_unavailable_retry_after`.
- Client side (ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`):
  `retry-logic.ts` parses `Retry-After` / `Retry-After-Ms` headers and the
  `retry_after` body field, but caps the applied delay at `maxDelayMs = 60000`
  (60 s). A multi-hour "come back online" wait is therefore not honoured as-is
  by the current client (see Q3).

## Desired change

1. Make the 429 local slot-exhaustion response carry `Retry-After` and
   `retry_after` (reuse `_get_slot_unavailable_retry_after`).
2. Make the router concurrency-limit 503 carry `Retry-After` and `retry_after`.
3. Audit the remaining "no models available" rejections (see Q2) and give each a
   consistent retry instruction, or explicitly record why it has none.
4. Update `proxy/README.md` and code comments to document the unified contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_exhausted_response` 429 branch (~line 2955),
  `_get_slot_unavailable_retry_after` (~line 2794), `_compute_retry_after` (~line 2257).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — concurrency-limit rejection (~line 1055).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_build_slot_exhaustion_response` (~line 570) as the
  reference implementation for the retry-hint contract.
- `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_error_code.py`, `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — extend/add retry-hint assertions.
- `proxy/README.md` — exhaustion / capacity-response contract section (~line 690).

## Related work

| Item | Relationship |
|------|-------------|
| LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO — Epic: Overnight remote-chain exhaustion | Related epic; the generic/time-window 503 retry contract was delivered by its children. This item covers the *remaining* capacity paths. |
| LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4 — Honest Retry-After: emit real provider availability windows | Predecessor: introduced truthful `retry_after`/`Retry-After` on the exhaustion 503. |
| LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G — Exhaustion 503: stable machine-readable error code | Predecessor: added `code` discriminators. |
| LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08 — Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real `retry_after` | Predecessor: bounds the hold by the retry timer. |
| LP-0MQHCG7FA005U886 — Strengthen Retry-After test assertion | Prior test-quality work on `Retry-After`. |
| LP-0MQS6MPK9000UIZK — Phase 2: Queue overflow rejection with Retry-After | Precedent: queue-overflow rejection already carries `Retry-After`. |
| ContextHub `WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W` / `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK` | Client-side recovery classifier/retry handling (separate repository) — decides how the retry timer is acted on, including the 60 s cap. |

## Risks & assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Scope overlaps the completed overnight-exhaustion epic, duplicating delivered work | Q1 confirms whether this item covers only the *remaining* paths or is superseded. |
| A retry hint on the concurrency-limit 503 could cause a retry storm | Use a conservative, documented bound; clients also apply upward jitter. |
| Changing the 429 body could break the existing `all_slots_exhausted` contract tests | Additive-only: the header/field are added, existing fields retained. |
| The client 60 s cap means a multi-hour wait is not honoured even with a correct hint | Q3 decides whether to align the client cap (ContextHub item) or accept the cap. |
| Scope creep (adding retry semantics to unrelated 4xx, e.g. compaction gate / single-flight) | Q2 bounds the set of responses in scope; extras become linked work items. |

Assumptions (to be confirmed):

- The proxy is the correct repository for this item; client recovery changes
  live in ContextHub (epic constraint).
- `Retry-After` is expressed as integer delta-seconds, consistent with all
  existing proxy responses.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / supersession):** This item (created 2026-09-16) predates the
  overnight-exhaustion epic LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO (created 2026-09-17), whose
  children already added `Retry-After` + `retry_after` + stable codes to the
  generic and time-window exhaustion 503. Which is intended?
  (a) Scope this item to the remaining proxy capacity rejections that lack a
  retry timer (429 local slot exhaustion, concurrency-limit 503) and audit the
  rest; (b) treat it as an end-to-end verification of the whole "no models
  available" retry contract on the proxy; (c) close it as superseded by the
  epic; (d) include the client-side ContextHub classifier in scope.
  **Recommended:** (a) — it is the only clearly undocumented gap and does not
  duplicate the epic.
  — **OPEN QUESTION** (no answer recorded; awaiting producer).
- **Q2 (which responses count as "no models available"):** Which rejections
  must carry a retry timer? (a) All fallback-chain exhaustion 503s, plus the
  429 local slot-exhaustion path, plus the router concurrency-limit 503;
  (b) only the "all providers exhausted" 503; (c) every 4xx/5xx that stops the
  request, including the compaction-gate 429 and the session single-flight 429.
  **Recommended:** (a) — these are the capacity-availability rejections; the
  compaction gate and single-flight are request-shape/duplicate-work signals,
  not missing capacity.
  — **OPEN QUESTION** (no answer recorded; awaiting producer).
- **Q3 (retry-horizon / client cap):** The ContextHub client caps an applied
  `Retry-After` at 60 s (`retry-logic.ts` `maxDelayMs = 60000`), so a truthful
  multi-hour overnight `retry_after` is not actually waited out by the client.
  Should this item (a) emit the true wait and raise the client cap via a linked
  ContextHub work item so the client sleeps until models return; or (b) emit a
  bounded wait (≤ 60 s) so the client retries periodically? **Recommended:**
  (a) — the seed intent is "retry when the models come back online", which a
  60 s cap cannot satisfy for multi-hour gaps; the client change is a linked
  ContextHub item.
  — **OPEN QUESTION** (no answer recorded; awaiting producer).

# Persist usage-limit quarantine and provider cooldowns across proxy restarts

## Problem statement

Provider availability state — the usage-limit account quarantine (`_usage_reset_at`) and the provider/entry cooldowns (`_provider_unavailable_until`) — lives only in module-level in-memory dicts, so every proxy restart wipes it. Each restart re-exposes an already-exhausted upstream account and the proxy emits fresh HTTP 429s until the quarantine is re-learned.

## Users

Proxy operator (and, indirectly, every agent/consumer routed through the proxy), who pays the cost of repeated upstream 429s and wasted fallback latency after each restart.

- **Operator story:** "As a proxy operator, I want upstream usage-limit quarantine and provider cooldown state to survive a proxy restart (mode switch, watchdog self-heal, manual `set-mode`), so that restarting does not re-expose an already-exhausted upstream account and generate repeated HTTP 429s."
- **Consumer story:** "As an agent routed through the proxy, I want the proxy to keep skipping an exhausted upstream after a restart, so my requests go straight to a working provider instead of burning a turn on a 429."

## Observed problem (evidence)

The 2026-09-25 `proxy-usage-analysis` window (24 h) logged 15 in-window `[remote] upstream error status=429` events, all from `opencode.ai/zen/go` with body `error.type = GoUsageLimitError`, `metadata.limitName = monthly`.

These are handled by the usage-limit reset quarantine ([LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ](LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ)), which sets `_usage_reset_at[account] = now + 30 days + 2 min`. The quarantine works while the process lives: 35,093 `usage_limit_reset_pending` skip lines were emitted, e.g. 499 skips in 10:04–10:32 and 648 in 11:04–13:10.

However `_usage_reset_at` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:90`) and `_provider_unavailable_until` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:44`) are module-level in-memory dicts with no persistence. The proxy restarted 12 times in the window; every restart wiped the quarantine, and each of the 15 429s lands 3–35 minutes after a restart with zero `usage_limit_reset_pending` skips in between:

| Gap | Skip lines | Restart before | 429 after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10:34–11:02 | 0 | 10:33:20 | 11:03:28 |
| 13:48–13:58 | 0 | 13:47:40 | 13:59:02 |

So the 429s are suppressed between restarts but recur after each restart re-exposes the exhausted `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` account.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  - `_provider_unavailable_until: dict[str, float]` (line 44) — provider/brand/entry/failure-domain key → epoch expiry. Mutated by `mark_provider_unavailable()` (line 1804) and read/lazily-expired by `_provider_cooldown_remaining()` / `_is_provider_unavailable()` (lines ~1860–1895).
  - `_provider_failure_count: dict[str, int]` (line 47) — consecutive-failure counter for exponential backoff; deliberately **not** in scope.
  - `_usage_reset_at: dict[str, float]` (line 90) — usage-limit account key → epoch expiry. Populated at lines ~4961 and ~6103 for `GoUsageLimitError` / `FreeUsageLimitError`; read/lazily-expired by `_usage_reset_remaining()` (line ~3663, used by the routing skip at lines 1668–1676 and 3465–3480). Keys come from `_usage_limit_account_key()` (line 3408, `api_key_env@<failure-domain>`), which itself derives from `_failure_domain_key()` (line 3295).
  - Both dicts are cleared by module import only; tests clear them in fixtures (e.g. `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_quarantine_diagnostics.py`).
- Existing persisted-state precedents in the proxy:
  - `proxy/proxy/grandfathering.py` — JSON state file `proxy/grandfathering-state.json` (beside `proxy/.mode`), written atomically via `tmp` + `os.replace` (`GrandfatheringRegistry.save`, line ~339) and loaded with corruption tolerance (`load`, line ~378).
  - `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `request_counts.json` / `token_counts.json` in `log_dir`, atomic `tmp.replace(path)`, corruption → empty dict.
  - `proxy/proxy/mode.py` — small companion state files beside `proxy/.mode` (`.mode.override-until`, `.mode.last-fast-switch`).
- Startup load hook: `_startup_launch_persistence_tasks()` in `proxy/proxy/server.py` (line ~772) calls `load_counts()` / `load_token_counts()`; provider restore should hook in alongside this.

## Desired change

Persist and restore on startup the two availability maps above:

- On mutation (`mark_provider_unavailable()`, and the two usage-limit quarantine assignments), write the current maps atomically to a JSON state file.
- On startup, load the file, drop already-expired entries (lazy/at-load), and log the number of restored quarantine and cooldown entries at INFO.
- Handle a missing, corrupt, or unparsable file without crashing (log and treat as empty, following `observability.load_counts` / `GrandfatheringRegistry.load`).
- Key entries stably so persisted keys remain valid across restarts (account key for `_usage_reset_at`, cooldown key for `_provider_unavailable_until`); persist absolute epoch expiries so wall-clock time is the source of truth across the restart boundary.
- Do **not** persist `_provider_failure_count` (backoff restarts at base on restart — acceptable and out of scope).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A usage-limit account quarantine set before a restart is still in force after the restart: the first routing decision after restore skips the affected provider with the existing `usage_limit_reset_pending` log line and makes **no** upstream request to it.
2. `_provider_unavailable_until` cooldowns likewise survive a restart and continue to be honoured (a cooling-down provider/entry is skipped; an expired entry is not).
3. Persisted state is written atomically (temp file + rename) and a missing, corrupt, or unparsable state file is handled safely — no crash, expired entries dropped at load, empty state treated as empty.
4. Startup logs the number of restored quarantine and cooldown entries.
5. Tests cover: set → persist → reload → skip for each map; expiry dropping at load; and corruption/missing-file handling. (Testing/validation criterion.)
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries (state-file location, restore-on-startup behaviour, scope boundary vs `_provider_failure_count`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the existing persisted-state patterns (`grandfathering.py` atomic JSON state beside `proxy/.mode`, or `observability.py` counts JSON in `log_dir`) rather than inventing a new mechanism.
- No new dependency; use stdlib `json` + `os.replace`.
- Restore is best-effort and must never block or fail proxy startup (log and continue on any error).
- Keep the change surgical: do not alter routing/quarantine semantics, only add persistence/restore. Restart-frequency reduction is out of scope.
- The proxy runs many concurrent sessions; writes happen on a cold path (a provider failing / a 429), so a synchronous atomic write on mutation is acceptable, but a write must not raise into the routing path.
- Do not persist `_provider_failure_count` or any other in-memory state (sibling-failure counters, local-400 streaks) — out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — add a state-file path helper + `load_provider_state()` / `save_provider_state()`; call save from `mark_provider_unavailable()` and the two `_usage_reset_at[...] = ...` sites; read both dicts in the loader.
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — call the provider-state loader from `_startup_launch_persistence_tasks()` (or an equivalent startup helper) so restore happens on every process start.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_state_persistence.py` (new) — set → persist → reload → skip; expiry and corruption handling.
- `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_quarantine_diagnostics.py` / `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` — likely need the new state file isolated/cleared in fixtures (or the loader pointed at a tmp path) so existing tests are not polluted by a real on-disk state file.

## Problem

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` decides whether to preserve the co-located llama-server across a `--restart` by comparing a sha256 of the RAW mode config file (`config-fast.yaml` / `config-cheap.yaml`) against the value stored in `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json`.

After the config dedup (LP-0MUI67ZNM008627E), the mode files are overlays and no longer contain base-inherited local-backend settings (for example `local_model_ctx_size`, `session_slot_pool_size`, `llama_server_port`). A change to `config.yaml` therefore no longer changes the mode-file hash, so a restart after a base change can wrongly PRESERVE a llama-server whose effective config actually changed (stale warm cache / wrong parallel slots).

## Proposed fix

Hash the MERGED config (base `config.yaml` + selected overlay) when computing the restart signature, reusing `proxy.config_merge.load_merged` (already used by `resolve_api_keys`). Add shell-test coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The restart signature is derived from the effective (merged) config, so a base-only change that affects the local backend forces a llama-server restart.
- An unchanged merged config still preserves the warm llama-server.
